semantic_correction.stem: During a skin assessment of an immobile hospitalized client, the RN finds intact nonblanchable redness over the sacrum. The client is currently lying supine. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Apply a moisture-barrier product to the intact redness and keep the client supine until the next scheduled repositioning time.
options.B: Reposition the client to relieve sacral pressure, initiate the facility pressure-injury prevention plan, and reassess the affected skin.
options.C: Place a folded pillow directly beneath the sacrum to cushion the reddened area while keeping the client centered in the supine position.
options.D: Document the nonblanchable redness and request a wound consultation before changing the client's position or relieving pressure.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly requires newly licensed RNs to perform skin assessment and implement measures to maintain skin/tissue integrity, identify complications of immobility such as skin breakdown, and evaluate responses to interventions that prevent immobility complications. AHRQ pressure-injury materials identify intact nonblanchable erythema over a bony prominence as a Stage 1 pressure injury and emphasize pressure redistribution/offloading and individualized prevention planning when pressure-related discoloration is identified. Because the client is currently lying directly on the affected sacral area, B is the uniquely best response: remove pressure from the site immediately through repositioning, activate the facility prevention plan and reassess the skin. A leaves the client on the pressure source while treating moisture rather than pressure. C places additional material directly beneath the affected bony prominence while maintaining the same pressure-bearing position. D delays immediate pressure relief while waiting for consultation. Therefore B is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: When intact nonblanchable redness is identified over a pressure-bearing bony prominence, relieve pressure promptly through repositioning/pressure redistribution, initiate the facility pressure-injury prevention plan and reassess rather than leaving the client on the affected area while waiting or applying an unrelated measure.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retired nursing-sensitive-indicator terminology because it was QI definition recall and overlapped existing quality-improvement constructs. Rebuilt the item around direct bedside recognition of pressure-related skin injury and immediate pressure redistribution using explicit NCSBN skin-integrity content and AHRQ prevention guidance. Removed the prior absolute-word and answer-length cues.

scope_exclusions.wound_staging_beyond_stage1: Not tested. The stem supplies intact nonblanchable redness and asks for the immediate nursing action, not a detailed wound-staging taxonomy.
scope_exclusions.fixed_repositioning_interval: Not universalized. Repositioning frequency and support-surface choices should follow individualized risk assessment and facility prevention protocols.
scope_exclusions.moisture_associated_skin_damage: Not the primary construct. The finding is localized nonblanchable sacral redness in an immobile client lying on the area, establishing pressure as the immediate hazard to relieve.
scope_exclusions.specialty_consultation: A wound/skin consultation may be appropriate, but it should not delay immediate pressure relief.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0726 tests unnecessary urinary-catheter removal. V2-Q0674 tests disaster reverse triage/discharge selection. V2-Q0520 tests missed-care escalation. V2-Q0770 tests immediate pressure redistribution after detecting intact nonblanchable sacral erythema. Targeted repository search returned no matching pressure-injury/offloading item before staging.

option_audit.A: Plausible skin-protection intervention but does not relieve the active pressure source and leaves the client supine on the affected area.
option_audit.B: Correct. It removes pressure promptly, initiates the prevention pathway and reassesses the skin response.
option_audit.C: Plausible cushioning strategy but keeps direct loading centered over the injured sacral area rather than offloading it.
option_audit.D: Plausible escalation/documentation response but delays the immediate pressure-relief intervention.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. The client is currently lying on an area with intact nonblanchable sacral redness. B alone immediately relieves pressure and begins the prevention plan. A/C maintain loading of the affected area, while D delays pressure relief.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. Correct option B is tied with C and all choices are within ten characters; the previous cue pattern is removed.
